Danish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French ponton, from Latin pōnto, from Latin pōns (“bridge”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [pʌŋˈtʌŋ]

Noun

[edit]

ponton (singular definite pontonen, plural indefinite pontoner)

  1. a pontoon (buoyant support)
  2. a pontoon (box to raise sunken vessel)
  3. a pontoon (float of seaplane)

Inflection

[edit]
Declension of ponton
common
gender 		singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative ponton pontonen pontoner pontonerne
genitive pontons pontonens pontoners pontonernes

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pontonbro (“pontoon bridge”)

References

[edit]
  • “ponton” in Den Danske Ordbog

[edit]

ponton

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French ponton, from Latin pontōnem (“ferryboat”), from pōns (“bridge”). By surface analysis, pont +‎ -on.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔ̃.tɔ̃/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Hérault)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

ponton m (plural pontons)

  1. (military) pontoon
  2. (nautical) pontoon (floating structure supporting a bridge or dock)
  3. (nautical) pontoon (the boat)

Related terms

[edit]
  • pont

Further reading

[edit]
  • “ponton”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Pronunciation

[edit]

  • Hyphenation: pon‧ton

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

ponton (plural pontonok)

  1. pontoon, a floating structure supporting a bridge or dock
  2. (military) pontoon, a flat-bottomed boat used as a support for a temporary bridge

Indonesian

[edit]
Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
ponton
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Dutch ponton (“pontoon”), from French ponton, from Middle French ponton, from Old French ponton, from Latin pontō, pontōnem (“ferryboat”), from pōns (“bridge”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈponton/ [ˈpon̪.t̪ɔn]
  • Rhymes: -onton
  • Syllabification: pon‧ton

Noun

[edit]

ponton (plural ponton-ponton)

  1. pontoon
    1. buoyant support for a temporary bridge, dock or landing stage
    2. pontoon bridge

Derived terms

[edit]
  • ponton isap
  • ponton penyeberangan

Further reading

[edit]
  • “ponton”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016
